newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER SHOWCASE-LAST ROAR FOR BOSKAMP AT ANDERLECHT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-LAST ROAR FOR BOSKAMP AT ANDERLECHT.

text.p: Dutchman Johan Boskamp is the kind of coach who can shout down a crowd without the help of a megaphone.
Often dubbed "Big Mouth" for the noise he makes and for his sharp wit and one-liners, Boskamp's booming voice has always been a potent weapon to reprimand or stir up players.
Now the familiar roar will sound one last time from the Anderlecht dug-out during the Belgian Cup final against Ekeren on Sunday.

After almost five years at the helm of Belgium's most prestigious and stylish club, Boskamp is moving to modest side Ghent where he has been given a free hand to fulfil his dream of setting up youth training projects.
A drained Boskamp, 48, had parted ways with Anderlecht a first time at the end of the 1994-1995 season after leading them to their third league title in three years.
But he was welcomed back with open arms when Anderlecht wanted him to take over from German Herbert Neumann, who was sacked after a disastrous start to the 1995-96 season.

Clearly ill at ease in tie and suit, Boskamp's rugged style and looks and his no-nonsense approach could not have contrasted more with his club's plush VIP boxes full of captains of industry and leading politicians.
As a player, Boskamp won two Dutch league titles with Feyenoord and a Belgian title with Molenbeek.
He started his successful coaching career in 1984 at Lierse, who were crowned new Belgian champions last Sunday, but pulled off his major successes at Anderlecht where he also lifted the 1994 Cup.
On Sunday, Boskamp will face another former Lierse coach in the Belgian Cup final.
Herman Helleputte, now Ekeren coach, will be bent on revenge for Lierse's 4-0 defeat by Anderlecht in the 1976 Cup final when he was still a player.
Victory on Sunday would also earn him a first coveted trophy.
"Every coach wants a prize list," Helleputte said. "They make your position strong during contract negotiations...now (my list) only says 'Cup final and nearly European'."
The soft-spoken former Lierse player was blamed for lacking leadership during his first spell at Ekeren and was replaced by Pole Stany Gzil at the end of 1995.
Like Boskamp, Helleputte was soon recalled, and he succeeded the sacked Gzil late last year.
Unlike Boskamp, he was forced to change his coaching style, dropping snooker and card sessions with his players.
Although Helleputte multiplied players' fines by 10, players said he had changed for the better and had gained authority.
"It hurt when I read that people said it was Club Med (holiday centre) here. That was unfair," Helleputte said.
